report.source_text: A mass slightly larger than 8 cm in diameter was found adjacent to the mid-thoracic esophagus. From above, the tissue surrounding the esophagus was detached and the tumor was excised. The resulting defect in the adventitia and muscular layer was extensive. A direct anastomosis was considered to be difficult, such that subtotal esophagectomy and esophagogastrostomy in the right thorax were performed.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 55-year-old woman presented with palpitations and swallowing discomfort. Chest radiographs revealed a smooth round middle mediastinal mass over 7 cm. Chest CT confirmed a large lobulated, homogenous mass compressing the esophagus. A biopsy was performed but histopathology report was not obtained. Surgical excision was done due to the tumor size and esophageal involvement, requiring subtotal esophagectomy and esophagogastrostomy. Histopathological examination of the excised tumor showed spindle-shaped cells with palisading nuclei and positive S100 staining, confirming a benign schwannoma diagnosis.
